solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nothing very large about article shaped like Easter gift?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the other letters are placed around the article

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of something big and empty wrapped round an item, apparently shaped like an Easter present.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is egg-shaped, and that rounded outline is described by this adjective; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Her caper disturbed a clergyman

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's prank upsets a vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister who gives sermons is a member of the clergy, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: German's recycled old fur

indicators.note: recycled means made over into something new, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German man is reusing an old fur coat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common German forename, so a German man may bear it; definition by example.

clue.text: Prisoner perhaps popular with friend

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
mate is a British word for a friend

explanation.surface: A jailbird who is well liked by a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in a jail or institution is a resident of it; 'perhaps' marks prisoner as one example.

clue.text: Arrival at home with illness by ten

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
flu is a common illness
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone gets home sick, with ten more to come.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflow of people or things is their coming in, so it is an arrival in numbers.

clue.text: Old woman one left in post

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman in slang
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly lady is the only one still working at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and parcels delivered by the postal service are called post in Britain; synonyms.

clue.text: State expressions of gratitude: an obsession

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you, so several are tas
a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: Someone declares that saying thank you has become a compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is the definition: an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The island south of mainland Australia is one of that country's six states.

clue.text: Tip up plain vase

parts.note: overt means plain or open to view
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: Instructions to knock over a simple vase.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something up is to upset it so it falls on its side; synonyms.

clue.text: Delicate insect crossing one manuscript

indicators.note: crossing means spanning across, so the insect stretches around the other letters

parts.note: a fly is an insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fragile bug walks across an old manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flimsy is thin and easily damaged, so it is delicate; synonyms.

clue.text: In Waterloo, pal lustily recalled Scottish resort

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters found are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a station bar at Waterloo, a friend heartily reminisced about a Scottish holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' picks LOOPALLU from 'Waterloo, pal lustily'; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: This fishing port on Loch Broom in the Highlands is a holiday town, so a Scottish resort.

clue.text: Skin condition not considered

definitions.meaning: an outbreak of red spots on the skin
done hastily without thought, as in a hasty decision

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an eruption on the skin and acting without careful thought; two unrelated senses.

clue.text: What to expect from competent handyman, thankfully

definitions.text: What to expect from competent handyman
definitions.meaning: a skilled worker turns out well-done work
a British idiom for luckily, as in 'it's just as well'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes well-finished work and idiomatically means fortunately, as in 'just as well we left early'.

clue.text: Hunter discovered holding bullock, close to ranch

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: found means discovered
an ox is a castrated bull, like a bullock

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word, its final letter

explanation.surface: A predator is found clutching a steer near the ranch.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of dog is kept to chase foxes, so it is a hunting animal.

clue.text: Poet's work was outstanding when recited

indicators.note: recited means spoken aloud, so the clue gives a word by its sound

parts.note: owed means was still due to be paid, outstanding

explanation.surface: A poem was exceptional when read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise for the poem, but here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric poem addressed to a subject is a typical piece of verse by a poet.

clue.text: Performs better than us at poly, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rival team surprisingly beats us at the polytechnic.
explanation.walkthrough: A poly is a polytechnic, a former type of British college.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent through superior play in a game is to perform better than them.

clue.text: One taking car from girl — a legal stipulation

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name
a rider is a clause added to a legal document

explanation.surface: A car thief steals from a young woman, and a law has something to say about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals a car to drive it for thrills takes the vehicle unlawfully.

clue.text: Small boy after party's slept

indicators.note: after says the small boy comes behind the party in the answer

parts.note: do is a party, and with the possessive gives do's
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A little lad has slept after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dossed' is British slang for slept rough or slept anywhere handy.
explanation.definitionFit: To doss is informal British for sleeping somewhere makeshift, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Place in short grass for standing

indicators.note: in says the first word goes inside the trimmed grass
short means cut off, so the last letter of the grass word is dropped

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
put means place

explanation.surface: Instructions to set someone in cropped grass for a standing position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' looks like part of the instructions, upright in the grass, but it is the definition, meaning status.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing is their reputation or status in others' eyes; synonyms.

clue.text: Weaselly creature losing head? Exactly!

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: a stoat is a member of the weasel family

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a weasel has been decapitated, and is told yes, precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops S from STOAT; the idiom is 'to a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'to a T' means precisely or perfectly, as in 'it fits you to a T'.

clue.text: Grey colour cell shows up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the hidden letters are read bottom to top, backwards
shows means displays, so the letters are on view within the words colour cell

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A greyish shade shows in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' finds URCE across 'colour cell'; 'up' turns it round in this down clue, the draft's 'shows up' split into its two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale greyish-beige shade of unbleached linen is a near-grey colour.

clue.text: More flexible about one's dealer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the more flexible word goes round the letter

parts.note: suppler means more flexible
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A merchant is described as more adaptable than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that provides goods for sale is a trader or vendor; synonyms.

clue.text: Business manager and former partner, each appearing on and off

parts.note: ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: on and off means alternately present, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: A manager and an ex keep turning up at the office now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Exec is the shortened form of executive, someone running a business.

clue.text: English planes carrying first of captives and exiles

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the planes contain the letter

parts.note: jets are aircraft

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: British aircraft fly prisoners and outcasts abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to throw them out of a place, so to expel; synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Yet competition ultimately free, strangely, with this?

definitions.text: Yet competition ultimately free, strangely, with this?

indicators.note: strangely means oddly, so the gathered letters are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark that a contest would be free if only one paid this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes N from 'competition'; with YET and FREE, 'strangely' rearranges them. The whole clue also hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge for taking part in a contest makes it no longer free, which is the clue's paradox.

clue.text: Answer certain to be readily available

parts.note: bound means certain, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: An answer is sure to turn up easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'certain to' reads naturally as 'bound to', which hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: To be plentiful or present in large numbers means being easy to come by.
